simple.meaning: יַצִּיב (yatstsîyb) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “fixed , sure ; concretely, certainty.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Daniel, beginning at Daniel 2:8. Its contexts include kingship, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יַצִּיב (H3330).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: יַצִּיב (yatstsîyb) / H3330 is traced through Daniel 2:8, Daniel 2:45, Daniel 3:24, Daniel 6:13 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The king answered, “I know of a certainty that you are trying to gain time, because you see the thing has gone from me.

timeline.evidenceText: The king answered, “I know of a certainty that you are trying to gain time, because you see the thing has gone from me.

Because you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it broke in pieces the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God has made known to the king what will happen hereafter. The dream is certain, and its interpretation sure.”
Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonished, and rose up in haste. He spoke and said to his counselors, “Didn’t we cast three men bound into the middle of the fire?”

Then they answered and said before the king, “That Daniel, who is of the children of the captivity of Judah, doesn’t respect you, O king, nor the decree that you have signed, but makes his petition three times a day.”
I came near to one of those who stood by, and asked him the truth concerning all this.
